$comment: Copy to ~/.pi/agent/geocine.json and edit. Project override: .pi/geocine.json (models merge by name). Selection is class-based: model map keys are just labels — the judge routes by classes, and the 'default' class marks the no-name fallback.

models.$comment: The model registry: every consultable model. Key each entry by the model it names (grok-4.6, qwen-27b), not by role — classes carry the capability semantics. classes are free-form tags (suggested: default, frontier, abliterated, cheap, fast, local, intelligent; capability tags like vision belong here too — they make the capability addressable as /consult @vision and visible to the router). rank breaks ties among models sharing a class (1 = first choice; three frontier models resolve @frontier to the best-ranked, and the route node prefers the lower rank when role and classes fit equally; unranked sorts last). A class works anywhere a model name does (consult tool, /consult @cheap) and the judge's route node picks the cheapest model whose classes cover the need — the standing goal is minimal LLM token spend. 'default' marks the fallback. The classes also drive the fabric for the MAIN session: when pi's picker lands on a model registered here, 'cheap' or 'local' arms the steering machinery (triage, escalate hints, gate nudges, tool guard) and 'local' opts it into the context keeper — whatever the provider. Availability: model choices (route node, approval picker, /consult, /models) exclude llama.cpp entries whose server is down or that pi's catalogue does not know; cloud entries are assumed reachable.

grok-4.6.$comment: Consult children are pi processes on the host, so they inherit auth automatically: OAuth providers via pi /login (~/.pi/agent/auth.json), API-key providers via the environment.
grok-4.6.role: hard debugging, root-cause analysis, and planning complex changes

gpt-5.6-luna.role: maximum-depth reasoning: subtle correctness bugs, algorithm design, and second opinions on frontier-level plans

qwen-27b.role: local dense 27B for coding, research, long-horizon agents, and native image/video

qwen-27b-uncensored.role: local permissive 27B for policy-sensitive work and high-risk security analysis
qwen-27b-uncensored.notes: Local-first permissive fallback with coding, vision, and reasoning.

abliterated-model.role: hosted fallback for policy-sensitive work and high-risk security analysis
abliterated-model.notes: Used when aligned models are likely to decline; ordinary analysis stays aligned.

deepseek-flash.role: super-fast cheap consult for quick answers, long-context work, and native image questions

muse-spark-1.3-contributor.role: discounted frontier-quality generalist for coding, 1M-token long-context work, and image questions
muse-spark-1.3-contributor.notes: Contributor tier of Muse Spark 1.3 ($0.10/$0.20 per Mtok); thinking capped at xhigh.

approval.$comment: Gate for LLM-invoked consult tool calls (user-typed /consult never asks). 'ask' prompts yes/no/always-allow/auto-all; 'judge' = the fabric's approve node auto-approves clearly justified, well-routed consults (>= approveThreshold) and falls back to asking when unsure — it never auto-denies, so denial labels stay human; 'auto' never prompts. Per-model: "autoApprove": true.

watchdog.$comment_judgeEveryTurn: With a judge configured, every turn with new tool activity gets a classifier verdict (catches drift, which counters cannot see; judge-only findings need judge.minConfidence). false = judge only verifies counter findings.
watchdog.$comment_baseUrl: Optional tier-1 LLM watchdog. Use a SECOND small model instance (e.g. Qwen 4B on another port), never the main single-slot server — a side request there evicts the main KV cache.

triage.$comment: Scores task hardness, refusal risk, and route for cheap workers. Policy-sensitive work can open a local-first abliterated lease; follow-ups dwell, clear topic changes return, ambiguity dwells, and manual model selection cancels the lease. Mid-task scoring can suggest an approval-gated consult. Verdicts log hop/dwell/return labels.

gate.$comment: Outcome gate (needs a configured judge). When the agent settles, the judge verifies the WORK PRODUCT — git diff read directly, test/lint outputs captured from what the agent already ran — and decides continue (nudge local on) / stop (done or needs you) / escalate (suggest consult). The same call also answers review flags in parallel: revert (checks regressed while diff grew), regression_risk, scope_creep, architectural_change, needs_more_tests, and needs_human — which suppresses nudges entirely at human decision points. maxNudgesPerTask caps automatic re-runs; a nudge starts a new local run, so nudges also require a cheap main model (registered classes cheap/local, else rescue.localProviders) — expensive models get the verdict as a status line only.

guard.$comment: Command guard (needs a configured judge). Destructive-looking shell commands (rm -rf, git reset --hard, force push, DROP TABLE, ...) pass a deterministic prefilter, then the judge decides against the current task: serves it, or collateral damage? Confident collateral damage is blocked with a reason the model sees. No judge = allow; pi's own tool approval remains the real gate.

toolGuard.$comment: Tool guard (needs a configured judge) — the fabric's call-level 'wasteful?' node, for CHEAP workers that are weak at tool use (registered classes cheap/local, else rescue.localProviders — local or budget cloud; frontier workers are never guarded). A deterministic prefilter tracks exact-call repeats, identical retries after a failure, and 3+ re-reads of the same file; only suspects reach the judge, which blocks confident thrash with a corrective reason the model reads (use recall / change the approach). Repeats after a state change (an edit, a fix) are allowed. Capped per task and cooled down between blocks; no judge = allow.

judge.$comment: System One classifier (TypeSafe Jev) — the decision fabric behind watchdog verdicts, task triage, the outcome gate, the command guard, the tool guard, recall reranking, compaction scoring, note expiry, the task-start memory gate, and prescreen: fast typed judgments with calibrated probabilities in ~100-500ms. Degrades gracefully — no API key, timeout, or 'enabled': false means every node falls back to its heuristic/LLM path. provider is a lib/judge backend id, so the classifier is swappable without touching call sites. minConfidence gates when a judge answer may overrule heuristics or act alone; maxCallsPerMinute is the fabric-wide rate cap (a decision loop degrades instead of hammering the API). Per-node call stats: /geocine judge.
judge.$comment_host: baseUrl is the host origin (evaluate path filled in) or a full evaluate URL. Official TypeSafe: https://api.typesafe.ai → POST /v1/systemone, model jev-latest, key TYPESAFE_API_KEY. OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai → POST /api/alpha/decisions, model ~typesafe/jev-latest (https://openrouter.ai/~typesafe/jev-latest), key OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Any other host: set baseUrl to its full evaluate URL. Swap model + apiKeyEnv to match the host.
judge.$comment_window: Jev's input window is 32k tokens (OpenRouter lists 32k; TypeSafe: 32k for state + the longest question). maxInputTokens clips serialized state so a large gate/prescreen payload cannot overflow it.
judge.$comment_trace: trace (default true) appends every answered judge call to <logDir>/judge-YYYY-MM.jsonl as one ready-to-train row: {ts, node, source, elapsedMs, context, schema, labels}. That is exactly the (context, schema, labels) shape a parallel-constrained-decoding head (e.g. Qwen2.5-1.5B) trains on — noul folded to a boolean field, choice/score to enum fields, answers to soft labels. source separates calibrated Jev labels from naive-llm ones, so weak labels can be filtered or down-weighted. Once trained, repoint provider at your own backend and decisions run free.
judge.$comment_fallback: fallback = the not-too-smart middle tier of the ladder Jev -> naive-llm -> heuristics: when Jev is unconfigured or a call fails, the same questions go to this OpenAI-compatible endpoint (a local server — free) as ONE temperature-0 JSON completion using the trace's own (context, schema) serialization (train/serve parity). Deliberately naive: no retries, no reasoning, probs clamped to 0.85 so it never out-shouts calibrated sources — and marked uncalibrated, so memory injections and digest drops refuse it outright. Same-origin guard: if this endpoint is the server currently serving the ACTIVE worker (loopback aliases count), the tier auto-disarms for that call — a side request on a single-slot llama.cpp server evicts the worker's KV cache and forces a full session re-prefill next turn. Point it at a SECOND small server (e.g. Qwen 4B on :8081) to keep the tier alive during local-worker sessions; leaving it on the worker's own port is safe but means heuristics-only whenever that worker is active.

context.$comment: context-keeper. Applies while the active picker model is a registered model classed 'local'; providers (default llama.cpp/lmstudio/ollama) is the fallback for models NOT in the registry. Everything else uses pi's built-in compaction untouched. mode: 'arc' = deterministic compaction digest (no model call, instant, recall recovers exact content), 'checkpoint' = LLM-written structured checkpoint, 'off' = pi default. compactAtTokens = compact EARLY while a context.providers provider is active — pi's own threshold (contextWindow - reserveTokens) is minutes of prompt re-ingest too late on a local server. idleCompactMinutes = also compact after N idle minutes past half the threshold (cost lands while nobody waits). pruner = ingestion-time head/tail trim of oversized bash/powershell outputs (cache-neutral: trimmed ONCE at capture, full output stashed for recall). recall = transcript search (exact regex primary, BM25 fallback) + full entry read-back; rerank = judge-score the fuzzy BM25 candidates and drop confidently-irrelevant ones before the model chases them (exact matches never reranked). notes = model-written facts pinned VERBATIM into every digest; reminderTokens = pre-compaction reminder lead so the model pins state before the cut (0 = off).
context.$comment_memory: judgeDigest (default true) = classifier-scored compaction: one judge call scores every non-user digest step drop / keep one-line / EXPAND VERBATIM — budget goes to what still matters instead of what is newest — and overflowing pinned notes are expired by staleness instead of age; no judge = plain deterministic digest. memory (default true) = task-start memory gate: once anything was compacted or pruned, each new task BM25-searches the raw transcript and the judge steers in confidently-relevant snippets (max 2) so a cheap worker does not re-derive earlier work; no judge = inject nothing. Hallucination containment: everything is verbatim transcript bytes (nothing generated), and the two context-MUTATING actions — memory injections and digest drops — act on calibrated-tier answers only; the naive-llm fallback may block/rerank/route but never puts words in the context or deletes kept steps.

qwen.$comment: Persisted Qwen thinking state set via /harness (auto mode + budget level) — survives restarts and /reload. imageLevel overrides the level for turns whose latest message carries an image (set via /harness image <level|inherit>; omit for no override).

harness.$comment: Transparent tool aliasing: advertise each model family's RL-trained tool names/schemas on the wire (qwen-code, grok-build, codex dialects) while pi stays canonical. Set false to disable renaming; the trained-tool equivalents (todo, web_fetch, web_search, apply_patch) stay registered either way.

pdf.$comment: read_pdf tool (pdf-reader extension, @firecrawl/pdf-inspector). maxChars caps one call's output — the tool fills whole pages, then names the omitted pages so the model fetches exactly what it needs next. maxSearchMatches caps `search` result lines.

web.$comment: Provider behind web_fetch/web_search. 'auto' = first available (tinyfish when its key is present, else builtin DuckDuckGo scrape; a keyed provider that errors mid-call falls back to builtin for that call). Pin 'tinyfish' or 'builtin' to force one — pinned providers surface their errors. tinyfishApiKey: literal key or '$VAR_NAME' env reference; TINYFISH_API_KEY env var also works.

rescue.$comment: Captures manual local->frontier /model switches as rescue episodes in the consult-log. /distill drafts a lesson from the last episode using distillModel (default: prescreen.model). localProviders doubles as the cheap-worker FALLBACK: a picker model registered in `models` is classified by its own classes (cheap/local arm the steering machinery — triage steers, gate nudges, tool guard); this list only decides for unregistered models. 'Local' means cheap, not physically local — budget cloud hosts (baseten, abliteration-ai) belong here too. The worker is never designated; it is whatever pi's model picker has active.
